ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in Figure 1, there is a circular paper with point O as the center and AB as the diameter. Point C is on the circle $\odot$O. Folding the circular paper along the diameter CF, point B falls on point D located on $\odot$O (not coinciding with point A). After unfolding the paper, connect CB, CD, and AD. Let CD intersect with diameter AB at point E. AD$\parallel$OC; as shown in Figure 2, when CD$\perp$AB, if OC＝2, what is the length of BC?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} From the fold, it is known that: $\angle ECO = \angle BCO$,\\
$\because OB = OC$,\\
$\therefore \angle OCB = \angle B$,\\
$\therefore \angle ECO = \angle OCB = \angle B$,\\
$\because CD \perp AB$,\\
$\therefore \angle ECO + \angle OCB + \angle B = 90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle ECO = \angle OCB = \angle B = 30^\circ$,\\
$\because OC = OB = 2$,\\
$\therefore OE = 1$,\\
$\therefore CE = \sqrt{3}$,\\
$\therefore BC = 2CE = 2\sqrt{3}$;\\
Hence, the length of BC is $BC = \boxed{2\sqrt{3}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are a total of three circular geometric diagrams in the figure, and the one used for the problem is the middle Figure 2. In Figure 2, AB is a horizontal diameter, and O is on AB as the center of the circle; C is below the circle, F is at the upper right of the circle, and C, O, F are collinear, indicating the crease diameter CF; D is at the upper left of the circle, CD is a vertical line segment and intersects AB at E, so Figure 2 shows CD ⟂ AB at E; CB, CD, AD are connected, and AD is parallel to the direction of OC. Reasoning: The folding is along diameter CF, that is, reflection along the line containing O and C, and B is mapped to D. Because C is on the crease, rays CB and CD are symmetric about OC, so ∠ECO = ∠BCO. Also OB and OC are both radii of the circle, so OB = OC, triangle OBC is an isosceles triangle, giving ∠BCO = ∠OBC. Thus ∠ECO = ∠BCO = ∠OBC. Since E, O, B are on the straight line AB, ∠OBC is ∠CBE in right triangle CBE; and ∠BCE = ∠ECO + ∠BCO. Also CD ⟂ AB, so triangle CBE is right-angled at E, and the sum of the two acute angles is 90°, that is, ∠ECO + ∠BCO + ∠OBC = 90°. The three angles are equal, so each angle is 30°. In right triangle OCE, OC = 2 is the hypotenuse, and ∠ECO = 30°, so OE = 1, CE = √(OC² − OE²) = √(4 − 1) = √3. Looking again at right triangle CBE, in which ∠CBE = 30°, CE is the side opposite 30°, so the hypotenuse BC = 2CE = 2√3.
